results.title: Preserving Hudson River State Hospital in Poughkeepsie, NY - Olmsted Network
results.snippet: A site of national significance, this remarkable Kirkbride hospital and its grounds— designed by Olmsted and Vaux— are currently at risk. Yvonne Laube and Robert Kirkbride February 14, 2025 ... A visit by students from Dr. Robert Kirkbride’s adaptive reuse studio at Parsons School of Design. Features the replacement roof after 2018 fire and partial installation of windows by developer. Photo by Yvonne Laube. At the Olmsted Network’s 2024 Annual Conference, Poughkeepsie’s Hudson River State Hospital (HRSH) was featured in a panel discussion, Preservation and Mental Health: Adapting Olmsted Designs to Modern Needs, about how communities are using and adapting state institutions and their landscapes.

results.title: Hudson River State Hospital - Wikipedia
results.snippet: The Hudson River State Hospital was a New York state psychiatric hospital that operated from 1873 until its closure in the early 2000s. The campus is notable for its main building, known as a "Kirkbride", which has been designated a National Historic Landmark due to its exemplary High Victorian Gothic architecture, the first use of that style for an American institutional building. results.title: The Legacy of the Hudson River State Hospital – A People’s Guide to the Hudson Valley
results.snippet: The facility, touted for its innovative approaches and size, received patients from all across the Hudson Valley and New York State. Other city and town hospitals sent their patients, coining the phrase “send them to Poughkeepsie.” Patient wings were overcrowded, possibly best exemplified by the partial use of the Clarence O’Cheney building for housing and worsened by the fact that only two of the female wards in the Kirkbride building were constructed due to poor planning.
